review_problems: Correction to rule S11D3-R1 predicate P3 (TC10): the 'terminal date' is a cutoff on APPLICATIONS (a certificate 'shall be issued only if application therefor is filed ... prior to' the date), not a sunset of the issuing power; on its face a timely application could still be acted on after the date. ledger_title: Regulations requiring compliance by contractors for Gov ernment supplies with the codes of fair competition for their respective industries prescribed. M 455 ; I NRA Codes 729 ; NRA Hand 117.
review_problems: Para. (2) end date 1943-06-30 is not proved as the end of payments 'made under the provisions of' NIRA: EO 9357 (effective 1943-07-01) transferred PWA functions together with 'the unexpended balances of the appropriations, allocations, or other funds' to the Federal Works Administrator, so liquidation payments from NIRA funds could continue after 1943 (later GSA, 1949). Record the date only as a bound (TC13): new Title II program authority ended 1943-06-30; last NIRA-fund payment date unknown; status unaffected.

Para. (2) ending ground is sound but should add the account-closing rule: no-year appropriation accounts are closed and balances canceled once purposes are carried out and no disbursement is made for two consecutive fiscal years (31 U.S.C. 1555), so no NIRA appropriation can fund a payment today; 31 U.S.C. 3526(c)(2) has a fraud exception and (c)(4)(A) leaves recovery from payees open, but neither gives the order a present object: any charge against a 1930s-40s officer is barred (28 U.S.C. 2415) and is a historical consequence (TC04/CR-4).
Confidence 'high' overstates para. (2): that no NIRA-fund payment remains is inferred from statutory termination and account-closing law, not records; medium is more accurate. Status unaffected.
what_remains_inferential: That no disbursing-officer payment "under the provisions of" NIRA was made after the 1940s is inferred from the termination of every NIRA payment authority, not from a records search; tax-refund payments for NIRA-year taxes would be time-barred but the refund-limitation statutes were not separately retrieved. review_problems: Gap closed (CR-1, lane test d): the producer left the committee lineage untraced (medium confidence). Official FR: the Federal Committee on Apprenticeship (FCA), the Secretary's apprenticeship committee, was renewed under FACA in 1996 with an employer/labor/public membership unlike EO 6750-C's (Office of Education, NRA, DOL) (61 FR 4491). Its charter 'expired on January 26, 1998' and a newly chartered FCRA 'succeeds' it (64 FR 3572, 1999). Since 1937, 29 U.S.C. 50a has given the Secretary independent power to 'appoint national advisory committees'. So even if the 1934 committee was the FCA's ancestor, any such body ended by charter expiry in 1998. Every later committee (FCRA, ACA) is a new act under 50a and FACA (TC08/TC11). All four CR-1 elements are met. On element 2, revival would need a new act, and a Secretary's charter under 50a is a separately authorized act, not EO 6750-C. Confidence on the committee can be raised.

Rule (1)'s certificate runs 'until and unless such certificate is revoked'. The footprint should record that this is a durable term with no own end, and test it under TC06. It fails TC06: the certificate's only consequence was an exception to wages/hours 'established in such code' (and agreements), which ended by 1936-04-01. A certificate under FLSA 14(a) must issue 'pursuant to regulations of the Secretary', and no current CFR recognizes NRA-era certificates (eCFR 0 hits). Status unaffected.

review_problems: Challenge (a): EO 11401 did NOT replace every clause. It replaced only the designation/composition and restated the name; it says EO 6868 "is modified to the extent provided herein", so paras. 3-6 survived 1968 (the producer agrees).

The 1987 endpoint used for para. 3 (powers and rulemaking) is a TRANSFER, not an end. Reorg. Plan No. 1 of 1987 (D.C. Code 1-1508.01) sec. III.B(1) transfers "all of the functions related to the powers and duties of the National Capital Housing Authority established pursuant to the [Alley Dwelling Act] and Presidential Executive Order 6868 of October 9, 1934, as amended" to DPAH, and sec. VI abolishes NCHA (eff. 1987-12-15). The plan names EO 6868 as the source of the transferred functions, and those functions then passed to DCHA (D.C. Code 6-202(a), 2000). So the functions continue under DPAH/DCHA, and the producer has not shown that they ended.
Abolishing NCHA does end paras. 2, 4 and 5 (officers, executive officer, annual report), because the actor is gone. Para. 6 ($500,000 allocation) is spent (TC07).

Open question: does DCHA (or the Mayor's designee under D.C. Code 6-101.02 and Mayor's Orders 88-30 / 88-161) still hold and exercise the EO-6868-derived power and rulemaking authority, or only powers under its own D.C. statute? ledger_title: Making Certain Changes in the Internal Revenue Collection Districts in the State of New York
review_problems: Challenge (g): the producer is right to reject NARA's lead. But the 1952 order does NOT make the boundaries "Treasury's own text": it creates Director offices for the collection districts "as presently constituted", so it presupposes the EO-defined districts and does not replace them (CR-7).

Ending supplied by the reviewer: Treasury Order 150-01 (60 FR, 1995-10-10), issued under the delegated sec. 7621 power, establishes 33 districts comprehensively, "fewer internal revenue regions and districts than designated in previous Orders", and supersedes the 1987 designation order. That is a comprehensive substitute for the whole subject. The 1998 restructuring (Pub. L. 105-206 sec. 1001) followed. Latest end: implementation of TO 150-01 (Commissioner-set dates, 1995 onward).
